displayName: Unity CLI (Unity 6000.0+, needs the com.unity.pipeline package)

setup.run: Install the Unity CLI (winget install Unity.CLI, brew install --cask unity-cli, or the installer script of the Unity CLI documentation) and check that `unity --version` answers in a new shell

An older package is upgraded with `unity pipeline upgrade --project-path "<project-root>"`. An editor that is already open loads a package only after it refreshes the project: bring its window forward and, when Auto Refresh is switched off (Hot Reload and similar plugins do that), run Assets > Refresh; until then the status form answers STATUS_PIPELINE_LOAD_PENDING

notes: <project-root> is the folder of the Unity project: the nearest folder at or above the working directory that holds ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt, and the folder of .unikit.json when none is found

<command> is two words, <group> <name>, for a package with groups and one word for an older package; the listings show which. Parameters of the command go after --, because a parameter named like a CLI option (a timeout, for one) is otherwise taken by the CLI

Pass the project path in every call. Never put --quiet on a tsv call: the rows vanish and the answer is empty with exit 0. A json or ndjson call takes --quiet, which changes nothing in the answer and hides a hint line on stderr

The answer of a call is an envelope and the command's own value is in data.result. The envelope's success means the command ran, not that the operation worked: read data.result whole, because a failure can also arrive as a success field of false, as an error with a code and no success field, as a status of unavailable or rejected, as capitalised Success and Error fields, as a reverted batch, or as failed tests in a test summary; only a thrown exception answers with exit 6. An ndjson answer may start with progress lines: read the last line. Line numbers in the diagnostics of a code run start at 0, those of a compile at 1

On Windows in Git Bash a scene-object path that starts with one slash is rewritten into a file path before the CLI sees it (/Name becomes C:/Program Files/Git/Name) and the editor answers that no such object exists: write the path without the leading slash (Parent/Child) or with two slashes, or address the object by its instance id

compile exits 0 on success, 6 when the code has errors or the time ran out, 7 when no editor answered - also for a few seconds after a compile or a Play Mode change, while the domain reloads: run the ready form and try once more before reporting the editor unavailable. A cold compile of a big project can take minutes: keep --timeout above it and give the shell call that long

The status form names Safe Mode (documented by Unity: STATUS_SAFE_MODE with the compile errors under data.instances[].safeMode.compileErrors; not reproduced by the measurement) and STATUS_PIPELINE_LOAD_PENDING (the package is in the manifest but the open editor has not loaded it yet). Status contacts every editor that is open on the machine: use it for diagnosis, not as a polling loop
Measured on CLI 1.0.0-beta.14 and package 0.9.1-exp.1 on 2026-10-25; the forms change between betas, so re-measure when the floors move
